intro_title: Write down what you want to do. Track it until it is done.
intro_subtitle: Every task is an issue. While you work you keep a pull request that says how far you got, and when the work is finished you accept it and the issue becomes done.
help_intro: Your flow: write an issue, start it, keep a pull request with your progress, accept it when finished.
help_repository: Repository — a separate area of work (a product, a course, a research topic). It owns its issues, pull requests, labels and milestones.
help_issue: Issue — one task: something to learn, build or finish. Status: open → in progress → done. A sub-issue is a smaller task inside a parent issue.
help_dependency: Prerequisite (depends_on) — issue A cannot start until issue B is done. It can point to an issue in another repository.
help_project: Project — a list of issues from any repositories that serve one goal.
help_concept: Concept — a topic (for example “caching”) that you can link from many issues. Links to a concept never block work.
help_pr: Pull request — your progress report on an issue you started. Edit it as often as you like while you work. Accepting it means the work is finished: the issue becomes done. IDIOS does not read or change Git or your files.
help_graph: Graph — shows how repositories, issues, projects and concepts are connected, and which issues are waiting on which.
help_notes: Notes — free text. A note can stay on its own, be attached to an issue or repository, or appear as a node in the graph.
help_seed: To try IDIOS with sample data, run idios-tui-demo. It uses its own database in ~/.idios/demo. The command `idios seed demo` adds the same sample data to the database you selected.
demo_workspace_notice: This is sample data. Changes are saved only in the demo database, not in your normal IDIOS database.
help_shortcuts: Ctrl+N new, / filter, ? help, g graph, r refresh. Tab and Shift+Tab switch sections; Ctrl+Tab or F6 moves focus to the buttons; Enter activates; Esc goes back; q quits.
settings_font_note: Font family and size are set in your terminal, not in IDIOS.
notes_empty: No notes yet. Choose “+ New note” to write one.
jobs_empty: No scheduled jobs yet. Choose “+ Add job” to create a one-time reminder, an interval timer or a daily, weekly or monthly schedule.
